Members of the onion family.Garlic: Garlic was fed to Egyptian pyramid builders, and an old claim says it was a wage perk. Its sharp smell comes from allicin, made only when a clove is crushed.
Members of the onion family.Leek: The leek is Wales's national emblem, worn on St David's Day. Its milder, sweeter flavor comes from long, blanched white shafts grown buried in soil.
Members of the onion family.Shallot: Shallots grow in clustered bulbs, not single ones, and French cooks prize them for sauces. They are sweeter and subtler than regular onions.
Members of the onion family.Chives: Chives are the smallest edible Allium species, and their purple pom-pom flowers are edible too. Gardeners plant them to deter pests.
Members of the onion family.Scallion: Scallions are onions picked young, before a bulb forms. In much of the U.S. green onion means the same thing; the white base and green tops are both eaten.
Members of the onion family.Ramps: Ramps are wild leeks that carpet Appalachian forests each spring. They take years to regrow after harvest, so overpicking has made them a conservation worry.
Members of the onion family.Red onion: Red onions get their color from anthocyanins, the same pigments found in red cabbage and berries. They are milder raw, so they top burgers and salads.
Members of the onion family.Pearl onion: Pearl onions are small, mild bulbs that are fiddly to peel, so cooks blanch them first. They are a classic in coq au vin and boeuf bourguignon.
Members of the onion family.Elephant garlic: Despite the name and giant cloves, elephant garlic is closer to a leek than true garlic. Its flavor is much milder, so it can be eaten almost like a vegetable.
Members of the onion family.Vidalia onion: Vidalia onions are legally grown only around Vidalia, Georgia. Low-sulfur soil makes them so sweet that some people eat them raw like apples.
Members of the onion family.Garlic scapes: Scapes are the curling flower stalks that hardneck garlic sends up in early summer. Growers cut them so the plant puts energy into the bulb; they taste like mild garlic.
Members of the onion family.Fennel: Fennel is in the carrot and parsley family, not the onion family. Its bulb and fronds taste of anise, and Greek legend says Prometheus carried fire in a fennel stalk.
Members of the onion family.Celery: Celery is an umbellifer, related to carrots and parsley, not alliums. The old myth that eating it burns more calories than it contains is untrue, though it is very low in calories.
Members of the onion family.Bok choy: Bok choy is a Chinese cabbage, so it belongs with the brassicas. It has crisp white stalks and dark leaves, and baby bok choy is a popular stir-fry green.
Members of the onion family.Kohlrabi: Kohlrabi looks like a root but is a swollen stem of the cabbage family. Its name is German for cabbage turnip, and it tastes like a sweet, crunchy broccoli stem.
Members of the onion family.Radish: Radish is a brassica, in the mustard family. Its peppery bite comes from the same compounds as mustard and wasabi, and some varieties are ready in about three weeks.
Members of the onion family.Turnip: Turnips belong to the cabbage family. Before pumpkins, Irish and Scottish people carved turnips into Halloween lanterns.
Members of the onion family.Parsnip: Parsnip is a carrot relative, not an onion. Its starch converts to sugar in cold ground, so winter frost makes it taste sweeter; it was a main sweetener before cane sugar.
Members of the onion family.Ginger: Ginger is a rhizome, an underground stem, from a tropical plant related to turmeric and cardamom. It has no connection to onions beyond being a pungent kitchen staple.
Members of the onion family.Lemongrass: Lemongrass is a tropical grass, not an allium. Its lemony scent comes from citral, the same compound found in lemon peel, and it flavors much Thai and Vietnamese cooking.
Members of the onion family.Asparagus: Asparagus is a lily-family plant, only a distant cousin of the Allium group. Its spears can grow several inches in a single day in warm spring weather.
Members of the onion family.Celeriac: Celeriac is a knobbly celery variety grown for its root. It looks rough, but peeled and mashed it tastes like celery crossed with parsley and potato.
Members of the onion family.Jicama: Jicama is a Mexican legume root, in the bean family. Its crisp, juicy white flesh is eaten raw, though the leaves and seeds of the plant are toxic.
Members of the onion family.Daikon: Daikon is a giant white radish, a brassica. Its name is Japanese for big root, and it is grated beside tempura and pickled for takuan.

Brandies.Cognac: Only brandy from the Cognac region of France, double-distilled in copper pot stills, can carry this name. The letters VS, VSOP and XO mark age.
Brandies.Armagnac: France's older brandy, distilled in Gascony since the 1300s, usually once in a column still, and often bottled by vintage year.
Brandies.Calvados: An apple or pear brandy from Normandy. Distillers often age it in oak for years, and a small glass mid-meal is the French trou normand.
Brandies.Pisco: A grape brandy made in Peru and Chile, which still dispute its origin. The Pisco Sour is the signature cocktail.
Brandies.Grappa: Italian brandy made from the pomace, the skins and seeds left after winemaking, so it is a way to use everything from the grape.
Brandies.Kirsch: A clear, dry brandy made from cherries and their crushed pits, which gives its faint almond note. Swiss fondue often includes a splash.
Brandies.Slivovitz: A plum brandy common across the Balkans and central Europe, often homemade, and treasured as a national drink in Serbia.
Brandies.Brandy de Jerez: A Spanish brandy from Andalusia, aged in sherry casks using the solera system of fractional blending, which gives it a sweet, nutty taste.
Brandies.Applejack: A strong American apple spirit, historically concentrated by freezing cider and removing the ice, and it was popular with colonial farmers.
Brandies.Poire Williams: A pear brandy from Alsace and Switzerland, made from Williams pears. Some bottles have a whole pear grown inside.
Brandies.Rakia: A fruit brandy across the Balkans, often plum or grape, offered to guests as a gesture of hospitality.
Brandies.Bourbon: American whiskey from at least 51 percent corn, not brandy, which is distilled from fruit.
Brandies.Scotch: Whisky from Scotland, made from grain and malted barley rather than fruit, so it isn't brandy.
Brandies.Rum: A spirit from sugarcane juice or molasses, a very different base from the fruit that brandy uses.
Brandies.Tequila: A spirit from blue agave, grown mostly in Jalisco, so it is a plant spirit, not a brandy.
Brandies.Mezcal: An agave spirit, usually made by roasting piñas in earthen pits, which gives it its smoke. Not fruit brandy.
Brandies.Gin: A neutral grain spirit flavored with juniper berries, so it is a flavored spirit and not a fruit brandy.
Brandies.Vodka: Distilled from grain or potatoes and filtered to be nearly flavorless, so it isn't brandy.
Brandies.Sake: Brewed from rice in a process closer to beer, not distilled, so it is not a brandy.
Brandies.Cachaça: Brazil's national spirit, distilled from fresh sugarcane juice, which makes it kin to rum rather than brandy.
Brandies.Baijiu: A fiery Chinese spirit from sorghum and other grains, and the world's most consumed spirit by volume. Not a brandy.
Brandies.Soju: A Korean spirit, traditionally from rice and now often from sweet potato or tapioca, and not made from fruit.
Brandies.Absinthe: A green anise and wormwood spirit, typically made from a neutral base spirit, not a fruit distillate, so not brandy.
Brandies.Aquavit: A Scandinavian spirit flavored with caraway or dill, made from grain or potato, not fruit.

Countries in South America.Brazil: The largest country in South America and the only one that speaks Portuguese. It holds most of the Amazon rainforest.
Countries in South America.Argentina: Home to Aconcagua, the tallest mountain outside Asia, at nearly 7,000 meters. Its Patagonia region is vast.
Countries in South America.Chile: A long, thin country, over 4,000 kilometers north to south, which holds the Atacama, one of the driest places on Earth.
Countries in South America.Peru: The Inca built Machu Picchu there in the 1400s. Peru also gave the world the potato.
Countries in South America.Colombia: The only South American country with coasts on both the Caribbean and the Pacific. It's named after Christopher Columbus.
Countries in South America.Venezuela: Home to Angel Falls, the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, at almost a kilometer high.
Countries in South America.Ecuador: The equator, 'ecuador' in Spanish, passes through it. It also owns the Galápagos Islands that inspired Darwin.
Countries in South America.Bolivia: Landlocked and high up: La Paz is the world's highest seat of government, and the Uyuni salt flat is vast.
Countries in South America.Paraguay: Landlocked, with two official languages: Spanish and Guaraní, which most Paraguayans speak.
Countries in South America.Uruguay: The smallest Spanish-speaking country in South America. In 2013 it became the first to fully legalize cannabis.
Countries in South America.Guyana: The only English-speaking country in South America, with Kaieteur Falls, one of the world's most powerful waterfalls.
Countries in South America.Suriname: Dutch is the official language, a legacy of colonial rule. It is among the world's most forested countries.
Countries in South America.Panama: Panama is in Central America, though it is linked to South America by land. Its canal splits the Americas.
Countries in South America.Mexico: Mexico is part of North America. The Aztec capital Tenochtitlan stood where Mexico City is today.
Countries in South America.Cuba: A Caribbean island, so it is part of North America, not South America. It's the largest island in the Caribbean.
Countries in South America.Costa Rica: A Central American country that abolished its army in 1948. Its name means 'rich coast'.
Countries in South America.Honduras: A Central American country with Copán, a great Maya city. It's in North America.
Countries in South America.Nicaragua: Central America's largest country, with the huge Lake Nicaragua, which even holds freshwater sharks, a famous myth.
Countries in South America.Spain: Spain is in Europe, though its language is spoken across most of South America, which causes the confusion.
Countries in South America.Portugal: A European nation, which colonized Brazil, making Portuguese the language of South America's largest country.
Countries in South America.Jamaica: An island in the Caribbean, in North America, famous for reggae and Usain Bolt.
Countries in South America.Guatemala: A Central American country with Tikal, the ruins of a Maya city. It's on the North American continent.
Countries in South America.Belize: The only English-speaking country in Central America, with the Great Blue Hole off its coast.
Countries in South America.El Salvador: Central America's smallest country, nicknamed 'land of volcanoes', and it adopted Bitcoin as legal tender in 2021.

Landmarks in the USA.Statue of Liberty: A gift from France dedicated in 1886, it was once copper-brown. Oxidation turned it the familiar green over about 30 years.
Landmarks in the USA.Golden Gate Bridge: Despite the name it is not gold. It is painted a color called international orange, and it opened in 1937.
Landmarks in the USA.Grand Canyon: The Colorado River carved this Arizona gorge, which is about 446 km long and up to a mile deep.
Landmarks in the USA.Mount Rushmore: Carved between 1927 and 1941, the presidents' faces sit in the Black Hills, land considered sacred by the Lakota.
Landmarks in the USA.Hoover Dam: Finished in 1936 on the Colorado River, it created Lake Mead, the largest reservoir in the US by volume.
Landmarks in the USA.Alcatraz: This island in San Francisco Bay served as a federal prison from 1934 to 1963, and held Al Capone for a time.
Landmarks in the USA.Space Needle: Built in under a year for Seattle's 1962 World's Fair, it stands 184 m tall and has a rotating restaurant level.
Landmarks in the USA.Gateway Arch: At 192 m, this stainless steel arch in St. Louis is the tallest man-made monument in the United States.
Landmarks in the USA.Times Square: New York's neon crossroads was renamed after The New York Times, and its New Year's Eve ball drop began in 1907.
Landmarks in the USA.Yellowstone: America's first national park, from 1872, sits atop a huge volcanic caldera and holds about half the world's geysers.
Landmarks in the USA.Lincoln Memorial: Its 36 outer columns represent the states in the Union when Lincoln died. The seated statue is carved from Georgia marble.
Landmarks in the USA.CN Tower: Toronto's tower was the world's tallest freestanding structure from 1976 until 2007, but it is in Canada.
Landmarks in the USA.Christ the Redeemer: Rio's 30 m statue, clad in soapstone tiles, is in Brazil. Lightning strikes it several times a year.
Landmarks in the USA.Chichen Itza: The Maya city's pyramid El Castillo casts a snake-shaped shadow at the equinox. It lies in Mexico, not the USA.
Landmarks in the USA.Machu Picchu: The Inca citadel in Peru was built around 1450 and was made world-famous after Hiram Bingham's visit in 1911.
Landmarks in the USA.Banff: Canada's oldest national park, created in 1885 in Alberta, grew out of hot springs found by railway workers.
Landmarks in the USA.Sydney Opera House: Its sail-like roof is covered in over a million tiles, and it was designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon.
Landmarks in the USA.Table Mountain: Cape Town's flat-topped peak is often draped in a cloud called the tablecloth. It is in South Africa.
Landmarks in the USA.Big Ben: London's famous clock tower bell, not an American landmark. Its tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012.
Landmarks in the USA.Teotihuacan: Mexico's ancient city had pyramids of the Sun and Moon. The Aztecs found it abandoned and named it City of the Gods.
Landmarks in the USA.Lake Louise: A trap: this turquoise lake is in Alberta, Canada. Its color comes from fine rock flour ground by glaciers.
Landmarks in the USA.Uluru: Australia's giant sandstone monolith is sacred to the Anangu people, and climbing it has been banned since 2019.
Landmarks in the USA.Petra: Jordan's rose-red city was carved into cliffs by the Nabataeans over 2,000 years ago, so it is far from the USA.
Landmarks in the USA.Golden Temple: Amritsar's Sikh shrine in India runs a free kitchen that feeds tens of thousands of visitors daily.

Chemists.Dmitri Mendeleev: His 1869 periodic table left gaps for elements nobody had found yet, and he predicted their properties well enough to be proven right.
Chemists.Antoine Lavoisier: He showed that burning is a reaction with oxygen and that mass is conserved. He was executed during the French Revolution.
Chemists.Robert Boyle: His 1661 book The Sceptical Chymist helped turn alchemy into chemistry. Boyle's law links a gas's pressure and its volume.
Chemists.Linus Pauling: The only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes, chemistry in 1954 and peace in 1962, and he championed vitamin C.
Chemists.John Dalton: This Quaker schoolteacher revived the atom as a scientific idea in 1803 and also described his own color blindness.
Chemists.Humphry Davy: He isolated sodium and potassium using electricity and invented a miner's safety lamp in 1815. He also loved laughing gas.
Chemists.Alfred Nobel: He invented dynamite, and his will funded the Nobel Prizes. Element 102, nobelium, is named after him.
Chemists.Amedeo Avogadro: His hypothesis says equal volumes of gas hold equal numbers of molecules. A famous constant, the mole count, bears his name.
Chemists.Dorothy Hodgkin: She mapped the structure of penicillin and insulin by X-ray crystallography, and won the 1964 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Chemists.Fritz Haber: His process for making ammonia from air fed billions of people through fertilizer. He also led Germany's chemical weapons program in World War One.
Chemists.Joseph Priestley: He discovered oxygen in 1774, and he also invented soda water. He is remembered as a chemist and a dissenting minister.
Chemists.Isaac Newton: Newton is a physicist and mathematician. He did dabble in alchemy privately, but his fame comes from gravity and motion.
Chemists.Charles Darwin: Darwin worked in natural history and biology, not chemistry. His voyage on the Beagle shaped his theory of evolution.
Chemists.Galileo Galilei: A physicist who spotted that Jupiter has moons and that the Moon has mountains, he used a telescope, not test tubes.
Chemists.Nikola Tesla: He worked on alternating current, wireless power and the induction motor, so he is an engineer and inventor, not a chemist.
Chemists.Carl Sagan: A television host and astronomer who made Cosmos a hit. He studied planets and the search for life, not chemical reactions.
Chemists.Gregor Mendel: A monk and pea-plant geneticist, he founded the study of heredity. Chemistry wasn't his field.
Chemists.Johannes Kepler: He worked out the laws of planetary motion from Tycho Brahe's data. He was an astronomer, not a chemist.
Chemists.Edwin Hubble: The astronomer who proved other galaxies exist and that the universe is expanding. The space telescope is named after him.
Chemists.Charles Babbage: He designed the Difference Engine and Analytical Engine, early mechanical computers, so he is a mathematician and inventor.
Chemists.Alan Turing: A mathematician who cracked Enigma and sketched the idea of a general computer, so he's not a chemist by trade.
Chemists.Stephen Hawking: He also modeled how chemical reactions can create animal stripes and spots, in a 1952 paper on morphogenesis.
Chemists.Jane Goodall: She is a primatologist who studies chimpanzees, so her field is biology and not chemistry.
Chemists.Ada Lovelace: She wrote notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine that include what's often called the first computer program. She was a mathematician.

Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Giant tortoise: The islands are named for these tortoises (galápago is old Spanish for them). Some live over a century, and shell shapes differ between islands.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Marine iguana: The only lizard that feeds in the sea, it dives for algae and sneezes out excess salt through special glands.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Blue-footed booby: Males show off their bright blue feet in courtship dances. The bluer the feet, the more attractive he looks to females.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Galápagos penguin: The only penguin that lives north of the equator, it survives thanks to the cold Humboldt Current. It's among the rarest penguins.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Darwin's finches: Beak shapes differ across the islands, matched to food, and helped inspire Darwin's thinking about evolution, though he didn't grasp it at the time.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Flightless cormorant: The world's only flightless cormorant, it lost its flight over generations because food lies in the sea, and its wings became tiny.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Sea lion: The Galápagos sea lion is playful, often approaches snorkelers, and is found nowhere else in such numbers. Pups bark to find mothers.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Land iguana: These yellowish iguanas eat prickly pear cactus, spines and all. They can go long periods without drinking.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Frigatebird: Males inflate a bright red throat pouch like a balloon to attract mates. Frigatebirds can stay aloft for days at a time.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Hammerhead shark: Schools of scalloped hammerheads gather near the northern islands, where the wide head helps spot prey and sense electric signals.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Sally Lightfoot crab: These bright red and orange crabs scuttle on volcanic rocks and are famous for being nimble and hard to catch.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Kangaroo: Kangaroos are native to Australia, far from the Galápagos. It's a marsupial of the Australian region.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Koala: Koalas live on Australia's eastern coast, eating eucalyptus. None are found anywhere near the Galápagos.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Polar bear: Polar bears are Arctic animals and the Galápagos sits on the equator. The islands do host penguins, but not bears.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Komodo dragon: Komodo dragons are native to a few Indonesian islands. The Galápagos has iguanas, but no monitor lizards.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Lemur: Lemurs are found only on Madagascar and nearby islands, far from the Galápagos in the Pacific.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Kiwi: The kiwi is a flightless bird of New Zealand. It's a trap because the Galápagos does have a flightless bird, the cormorant.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Gorilla: Gorillas live in African forests. The Galápagos had no native land mammals apart from a few rodents and bats.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Tiger: Tigers are Asian big cats. The Galápagos never had native big predators, which helps explain why the animals are fearless of people.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Moose: Moose are northern forest animals of North America and Eurasia, with no place on the equatorial Galápagos.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Emu: The emu is Australia's giant flightless bird. The Galápagos has its own flightless bird, the cormorant, but no emus.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Tasmanian devil: This marsupial is found wild only in Tasmania, Australia, far from the Galápagos.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Puffin: Puffins nest in cold North Atlantic waters. The Galápagos is near the equator, where seabirds include boobies.
Animals of the Galápagos Islands.Giant panda: Giant pandas live in the bamboo forests of central China. Not found in the Galápagos.

Lord of the Rings characters.Frodo: Elijah Wood's hobbit carries the One Ring to Mount Doom; the three films were all shot back to back in New Zealand over about 15 months.
Lord of the Rings characters.Gandalf: Ian McKellen played the wizard, whose name Tolkien took from a list of dwarf names in an Old Norse poem.
Lord of the Rings characters.Aragorn: Viggo Mortensen reportedly broke two toes kicking a helmet in a take, and that painful scream stayed in The Two Towers.
Lord of the Rings characters.Legolas: Orlando Bloom's elf is a Woodland Realm archer; he is one of the Fellowship's nine members who are said to outlive the humans.
Lord of the Rings characters.Gimli: The dwarf is played by John Rhys-Davies, who also voiced Treebeard the Ent in the same film trilogy.
Lord of the Rings characters.Samwise: Sam Gamgee, the gardener who carries Frodo up Mount Doom, was played by Sean Astin; Tolkien called him the real hero of the story.
Lord of the Rings characters.Gollum: Andy Serkis's performance, captured on set with motion capture, helped make Gollum a pioneering digital character in 2002.
Lord of the Rings characters.Sauron: The Dark Lord appears in the films mostly as a flaming eye and as armor, since his body was lost with the Ring.
Lord of the Rings characters.Saruman: Christopher Lee, who played the white wizard, actually met Tolkien once and read The Lord of the Rings every year.
Lord of the Rings characters.Boromir: Sean Bean's 'One does not simply walk into Mordor' became an enormous internet meme long after the film.
Lord of the Rings characters.Arwen: Liv Tyler's elf has a much bigger part in the films than in the books, where she appears mostly in appendices.
Lord of the Rings characters.Pippin: Billy Boyd, who plays Pippin, sang 'The Edge of Night' himself in Return of the King, a song that he reportedly wrote part of.
Lord of the Rings characters.Treebeard: The ancient Ent speaks slowly and was voiced by John Rhys-Davies, the actor who plays Gimli too.
Lord of the Rings characters.Dumbledore: He's the white-bearded wizard of Hogwarts, not Middle-earth, which makes him a handy lookalike trap for Gandalf.
Lord of the Rings characters.Hagrid: Hagrid is Hogwarts' half-giant groundskeeper in Harry Potter, not part of Tolkien's world.
Lord of the Rings characters.Aslan: Aslan is the lion of Narnia, written by C.S. Lewis, a close friend of Tolkien in the Inklings writers' group.
Lord of the Rings characters.Mr. Tumnus: Tumnus is the faun who meets Lucy in The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, which belongs to Narnia.
Lord of the Rings characters.Obi-Wan Kenobi: He's the Jedi of Star Wars, played by Alec Guinness and Ewan McGregor, not a Middle-earth resident.
Lord of the Rings characters.Merlin: Merlin is the wizard of Arthurian legend, not of Middle-earth, though Gandalf was partly inspired by such wizard figures.
Lord of the Rings characters.Jon Snow: Kit Harington's Jon Snow belongs to Game of Thrones, a different fantasy saga.
Lord of the Rings characters.Daenerys: Daenerys Targaryen is the dragon queen of Game of Thrones, not of Middle-earth.
Lord of the Rings characters.Tyrion: Peter Dinklage won several Emmys for playing Tyrion Lannister in Game of Thrones, not in Tolkien's tales.
Lord of the Rings characters.Geralt: Geralt of Rivia is the monster hunter of The Witcher, from the books by Andrzej Sapkowski, not Tolkien.
Lord of the Rings characters.Dobby: Dobby is the freed house-elf of Harry Potter, and he's not related to Tolkien's elves.

Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Dorothy: Judy Garland was 16 when she played Dorothy, and the 1939 film's 'Over the Rainbow' won the Oscar for Best Original Song.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Toto: Toto was played by a Cairn terrier named Terry, who was paid more per week than many of the Munchkin actors.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Scarecrow: Ray Bolger played him, and had wanted the Tin Man role, but was cast as the Scarecrow.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Tin Man: Buddy Ebsen was first cast but became ill from the aluminum dust in the makeup, and Jack Haley replaced him.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Cowardly Lion: Bert Lahr's lion costume was made of real lion fur and weighed about 90 pounds under hot studio lights.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Glinda: The Good Witch of the North was played by Billie Burke, who arrived in a bubble and wore a huge pink gown.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Wicked Witch: Margaret Hamilton was burned in a fire-and-smoke accident while filming her exit from Munchkinland, and the green makeup was toxic.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).The Wizard: Frank Morgan played five roles, including the Wizard, the carriage driver and the doorman of the Emerald City.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Auntie Em: Clara Blandick played Dorothy's stern but loving aunt in the black-and-white Kansas scenes.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Uncle Henry: Charley Grapewin played the farmer who tries to calm Dorothy, in the Kansas scenes before the tornado.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Alice: Alice is the girl from Lewis Carroll's Wonderland, not Oz, though both tales involve a girl falling into a magical world.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Mad Hatter: The Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Wonderland, not Oz.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Cheshire Cat: The grinning cat that vanishes is from Alice in Wonderland, not Oz.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).White Rabbit: The White Rabbit is the one Alice follows, in Wonderland, not Oz.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Peter Pan: Peter Pan is the boy who never grows up, from Neverland, not Oz.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Tinker Bell: Tinker Bell is Peter Pan's fairy, and fairy dust belongs to Neverland, not Oz.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Captain Hook: Hook is Peter Pan's pirate enemy, not an Oz character.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Pinocchio: Pinocchio is Geppetto's wooden puppet from Italian author Carlo Collodi's tale, not Oz.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Jiminy Cricket: Jiminy is Pinocchio's conscience in Disney's film, not part of Oz.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Aslan: Aslan is the lion of Narnia, not the Cowardly Lion of Oz.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Mary Poppins: Mary Poppins is a magical nanny from London, not Oz, though she also flies with an umbrella.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Willy Wonka: Willy Wonka runs a chocolate factory in Roald Dahl's story, not Oz.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Geppetto: Geppetto is the woodcarver who made Pinocchio, not an Oz character.
Characters in The Wizard of Oz (1939).Queen of Hearts: The Queen of Hearts shouts 'Off with their heads!' in Wonderland, not Oz.

Films and shows set in Paris.Ratatouille: Pixar's rat chef Remy cooks in a Paris kitchen, and the film's dish was made by chef Thomas Keller, who consulted for it.
Films and shows set in Paris.Amelie: Audrey Tautou's shy waitress works at the Cafe des 2 Moulins in Montmartre, a real cafe you can still visit today.
Films and shows set in Paris.Midnight in Paris: Woody Allen's time-travel romance sends a writer to 1920s Paris to meet Hemingway and Fitzgerald; it won him an Oscar for screenplay.
Films and shows set in Paris.Moulin Rouge!: Baz Luhrmann's 2001 musical set in the Montmartre cabaret is built from mashed-up pop songs, and Nicole Kidman sang her own parts.
Films and shows set in Paris.An American in Paris: Gene Kelly's 1951 musical won Best Picture, and its lavish ballet finale of nearly twenty minutes set to Gershwin cost a fortune.
Films and shows set in Paris.The Aristocats: Disney's 1970 cat caper through Paris was the last animated film Walt Disney personally approved before his death.
Films and shows set in Paris.Hugo: Scorsese's 3D film is set in a Paris train station, and it is a love letter to real film pioneer Georges Melies.
Films and shows set in Paris.Les Miserables: Victor Hugo's novel follows the ex-convict Jean Valjean through Paris and the 1832 June Rebellion; its stage musical is among the longest-running ever.
Films and shows set in Paris.Before Sunset: Ethan Hawke and Julie Delpy reunite in Paris nine years later, and the film unfolds in nearly real time, in about 80 minutes.
Films and shows set in Paris.Emily in Paris: Netflix's comedy about an American marketer was a global hit, though many French viewers found its Paris a pile of clichés.
Films and shows set in Paris.Roman Holiday: Trap: that's Rome, not Paris. Audrey Hepburn won her only competitive Oscar for playing the runaway princess.
Films and shows set in Paris.Notting Hill: A London story: the film's famous blue door sold at auction, and the house's owners later painted theirs black.
Films and shows set in Paris.Lost in Translation: Set in Tokyo, not Paris. Sofia Coppola shot it in about a month, and what Bill Murray whispers at the end was never scripted.
Films and shows set in Paris.Casablanca: Despite its Paris flashbacks, it takes place in Morocco, and the famous 'Play it again, Sam' line is never actually spoken.
Films and shows set in Paris.In Bruges: Two hitmen hide out in a Belgian canal city, not Paris; Bruges's medieval center is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

Beatles songs.Hey Jude: Paul McCartney wrote it to comfort John Lennon's son Julian during his parents' divorce, and at over seven minutes it was a long single.
Beatles songs.Yesterday: McCartney dreamed the melody and first called it 'Scrambled Eggs'. It is among the most-covered songs ever.
Beatles songs.Let It Be: McCartney wrote it after a dream of his late mother, Mary, who told him to 'let it be', and it was the title of their last film.
Beatles songs.Help!: Lennon later said it was a real cry for help, written when fame was overwhelming him, though it sounds like upbeat pop.
Beatles songs.Yellow Submarine: Ringo sings this children's song, and it inspired a 1968 psychedelic animated film.
Beatles songs.Penny Lane: A real Liverpool street, near where both Lennon and McCartney grew up, and its bright piccolo trumpet solo was played by David Mason.
Beatles songs.Something: George Harrison wrote it, and Frank Sinatra called it his favorite Lennon-McCartney song, though it was in fact Harrison's.
Beatles songs.Blackbird: McCartney wrote it in 1968 as a response to the American civil rights struggle, and the ticking you hear is a metronome.
Beatles songs.Come Together: Lennon wrote it for Timothy Leary's campaign, and its opening line was borrowed from Chuck Berry, which led to a lawsuit.
Beatles songs.Eleanor Rigby: It is performed by McCartney with a string octet and no other Beatles playing, with a gravestone in Liverpool bearing the same name.
Beatles songs.Here Comes the Sun: Harrison wrote it in Eric Clapton's garden while skipping a tedious business meeting, and it is now the band's most-streamed song.
Beatles songs.Ticket to Ride: Often called a proto-heavy-metal song for its thudding drums and riff. McCartney played the lead guitar part, unusually.
Beatles songs.Get Back: The song was played live during their 1969 rooftop concert in London, which was the band's final public performance.
Beatles songs.Imagine: Not the Beatles: John Lennon's 1971 solo song, and its call to picture a world without borders makes it a peace anthem for many.
Beatles songs.My Sweet Lord: Not a Beatles song: George Harrison's 1970 solo hit was ruled to have unconsciously copied 'He's So Fine' in a famous lawsuit.
Beatles songs.Bohemian Rhapsody: Queen's six-minute 1975 opera-rock epic has no Beatles link, though it also broke the single-length rules of its day.
Beatles songs.Satisfaction: The Rolling Stones' 1965 hit, whose riff came to Keith Richards in his sleep, so he recorded it on a cassette before going back to bed.
Beatles songs.Wonderwall: Oasis released it in 1995 and are famous Beatles devotees, but the song is by Noel Gallagher, not the Beatles.
Beatles songs.Hotel California: The Eagles' 1976 song, famed for its long twin-guitar outro. It is a rival California rock band's hit, not the Beatles'.
Beatles songs.Paint It Black: A Rolling Stones hit from 1966, with Brian Jones playing sitar, the Stones' answer to the Beatles' Indian-influenced sounds.
Beatles songs.Jumpin' Jack Flash: A Rolling Stones hit from 1968 that marked their return to hard rock after a psychedelic phase.
Beatles songs.Live and Let Die: McCartney and Wings recorded this James Bond theme in 1973, so a Beatle is on it, but it is not a Beatles song.
Beatles songs.Waterloo: ABBA's song won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest and launched their global career, and has no Beatles tie.
Beatles songs.Respect: Aretha Franklin's 1967 version of Otis Redding's song made it a feminist anthem, and it isn't a Beatles song.

Famous drummers.Lars Ulrich: The Danish-born co-founder of Metallica, with double kick drum thunder.
Famous drummers.Travis Barker: Blink-182's drummer, who has played with many stars, and is known for lightning-quick fills.

Words that go before 'band'.Rubber: A rubber band's stretch comes from long polymer chains. Stephen Perry of London patented the first one in 1845.
Words that go before 'band'.Boy: Boy bands like New Kids on the Block and Backstreet Boys dominated pop charts in the 1980s and 90s.
Words that go before 'band'.Rock: A rock band is built around guitars, bass and drums. The classic four-piece lineup was cemented by the Beatles.
Words that go before 'band'.Brass: A brass band plays only brass and percussion instruments. Brass banding is a strong working-class tradition in northern England.
Words that go before 'band'.Marching: Marching bands play while moving, with traditions from military music. Sousa wrote famous marches for the US Marine Band.
Words that go before 'band'.Jazz: A jazz band can be a small combo or a big band. The earliest groups were in New Orleans in the early 1900s.
Words that go before 'band'.Head: A headband keeps hair or sweat out of your eyes. Tennis star Bjorn Borg made the terry-cloth one a fashion statement.
Words that go before 'band'.Arm: An armband can mark an official or a mourner. Armbands are also inflatable swim aids for toddlers.
Words that go before 'band'.Wrist: A wristband can be a fitness tracker or concert access pass. Livestrong wristbands in 2004 launched a silicone craze.
Words that go before 'band'.Hair: A hairband holds your hair in place. Alice bands are named after Alice in Wonderland illustrations.
Words that go before 'band'.Broad: Broadband refers to high-speed internet with a wide range of frequencies, in contrast to slow dial-up connections.
Words that go before 'band'.Big: A big band is a large jazz orchestra, and the swing era in the 1930s and 40s made Count Basie and Duke Ellington famous.
Words that go before 'band'.Steel: A steel band plays pitched drums made from oil barrels. It was invented in Trinidad and Tobago in the 1930s and 40s.
Words that go before 'band'.Pencil: Pencil band isn't a word. A pencil case and pencil sharpener are, though pencils actually contain graphite, never lead.
Words that go before 'band'.Choir: Choir band isn't a phrase. Choirs sing, often without instruments, while bands play instruments.
Words that go before 'band'.Note: Note band isn't a word. Notes belong to a band's music, but the two words don't join up.
Words that go before 'band'.Orchestra: Orchestra band isn't a pair. An orchestra is a larger group with strings, while a band is mostly winds and percussion.
Words that go before 'band'.Cello: Cello band isn't a standard term. Cellos usually sit in an orchestra's string section or a string quartet.
Words that go before 'band'.Piano: Piano band isn't a phrase, though pianos often join bands. A piano trio is a different kind of group.
Words that go before 'band'.Tooth: Toothband isn't a word. Toothbrush, toothpaste and toothpick are, and braces use bands, but they're called rubber bands.
Words that go before 'band'.Tune: Tune band doesn't exist. Tune up, tune in, tune out all do.
Words that go before 'band'.Song: Songband isn't a word, though songbird is. Birds that sing are a separate family from groups of musicians.
Words that go before 'band'.Lamp: Lampband isn't a word. Lampshade and lamplight are, but lamps have no band.
Words that go before 'band'.Shoe: Shoeband isn't a word. Shoelace and shoehorn are, but shoes use laces, not bands.

Pink Floyd albums.Atom Heart Mother: The 1970 album has a cow on the cover with no title or band name. It features a suite with a brass section and choir.
Pink Floyd albums.The Final Cut: The 1983 album was the last with Roger Waters. It's subtitled A Requiem for the Post War Dream.
Pink Floyd albums.Ummagumma: A 1969 double album, half live and half experimental solo pieces by each member. The title is slang from Cambridge.
Pink Floyd albums.Obscured by Clouds: A 1972 soundtrack for the French film La Vallée. It was recorded quickly at a French chateau.
Pink Floyd albums.Abbey Road: A Beatles album from 1969. Pink Floyd also recorded at EMI's Abbey Road studios, but this title isn't theirs.
Pink Floyd albums.Revolver: A 1966 Beatles album. Pink Floyd's Piper at the Gates of Dawn was recorded in the same studio a year later.
Pink Floyd albums.Led Zeppelin IV: A 1971 album by Led Zeppelin, with Stairway to Heaven. It's from a different band.
Pink Floyd albums.Physical Graffiti: Led Zeppelin's 1975 double album. The cover shows a New York tenement with windows that change.
Pink Floyd albums.Rumours: A 1977 Fleetwood Mac album, which came out the same year as Animals. It's a different band.
Pink Floyd albums.Hotel California: The Eagles' 1976 album. Its title track is among the best-known songs of its era.
Pink Floyd albums.Back in Black: AC/DC's 1980 album, a tribute to Bon Scott. It is one of the best-selling albums of all time.
Pink Floyd albums.Nevermind: Nirvana's 1991 album, with a baby swimming after a dollar bill on the cover. It's not by Pink Floyd.
Pink Floyd albums.OK Computer: Radiohead's 1997 album, which sounds more art-rock than the Floyd of the 70s. It isn't theirs, though many saw it as a spiritual successor.
Pink Floyd albums.The Joshua Tree: U2's 1987 album, named after a desert tree. It is by U2.
Pink Floyd albums.Born to Run: Bruce Springsteen's 1975 album, which made him a star. It's not by Pink Floyd.
Pink Floyd albums.Thriller: Michael Jackson's 1982 album. Pink Floyd's The Wall came out three years earlier.
Pink Floyd albums.Tommy: The Who's 1969 rock opera. It is also a concept album, but not Floyd's.
Pink Floyd albums.Pet Sounds: The Beach Boys' 1966 album, hugely influential to the Beatles. It is not Pink Floyd's.

Music abbreviations.DJ: Short for disc jockey, a term journalist Walter Winchell is credited with in 1935, for someone who rides records the way a jockey rides horses.
Music abbreviations.MC: It stands for master of ceremonies, and in hip-hop it came to mean the rapper who rocks the crowd, while the DJ spins the beats.
Music abbreviations.CD: The compact disc launched in 1982, and Billy Joel's 52nd Street was among the first albums pressed on it.
Music abbreviations.LP: Columbia introduced the long-playing record in 1948, which held about 22 minutes per side, far more than the old 78s.
Music abbreviations.EP: An extended play sits between a single and an album, typically four to six songs, and the term goes back to 1950s vinyl.
Music abbreviations.BPM: Beats per minute measures tempo, and house music usually sits near 120 to 130, close to a brisk walking pace.
Music abbreviations.MIDI: Musical Instrument Digital Interface, from 1983, lets synths and computers talk, yet a MIDI file stores notes, not actual sound.
Music abbreviations.MTV: Music Television launched on August 1, 1981, and its first video was The Buggles' Video Killed the Radio Star.
Music abbreviations.VMA: MTV's Video Music Awards began in 1984, and winners take home a statue of an astronaut, the Moon Person.
Music abbreviations.A&R: Artists and repertoire is the label department that scouts new talent and matches singers with songs, as with the staff who signed many famous acts.
Music abbreviations.CEO: Chief executive officer is the top job at a company, and while music labels have them, the abbreviation is not itself musical.
Music abbreviations.NASA: Founded in 1958, the US space agency is an acronym, said as a word, and has nothing musical about it, though it has sent a golden record into space.
Music abbreviations.FBI: The Federal Bureau of Investigation was founded in 1908, and the abbreviation is not tied to music, though it did once investigate the song Louie Louie.
Music abbreviations.DIY: Do-it-yourself is a craft and punk idea, but not a music abbreviation as such, as DIY ethos is often how small bands put out records.
Music abbreviations.ASAP: It means as soon as possible, and it can be said as a word, ay-sap, which is how many people pronounce it.
Music abbreviations.ATM: An automated teller machine, with the first one reportedly installed by Barclays in London in 1967.
Music abbreviations.GPS: The Global Positioning System uses a constellation of about 30 satellites, and its clocks must be corrected for relativity.
Music abbreviations.PDF: Adobe created the Portable Document Format in 1993 so documents would look the same on any computer.
Music abbreviations.BBQ: Barbecue is likely from the Taino word barbacoa, and it is a food abbreviation, not a music one.
Music abbreviations.DVD: Digital versatile disc is a video and data format that arrived in the 1990s, and it is not strictly a music term.
Music abbreviations.FAQ: Frequently asked questions began as a way to answer newcomers on 1980s online forums, and it is a web term, not a music one.
Music abbreviations.LOL: Laughing out loud was added to the Oxford English Dictionary in 2011, but it is a chat term, not a musical one.
Music abbreviations.HTML: HyperText Markup Language was invented by Tim Berners-Lee around 1990, and it is the building block of web pages.
Music abbreviations.RSVP: It comes from French répondez s'il vous plaît, meaning please reply, and it is an invitation term, not a musical one.

Sports played on ice.Ice hockey: Ice hockey's puck is frozen before games so it slides rather than bounces, and the NHL's Stanley Cup dates to 1893.
Sports played on ice.Curling: Curling stones are made from rare granite from Ailsa Craig, a Scottish island, and sweeping works by slightly melting the ice ahead of the stone.
Sports played on ice.Figure skating: Quadruple jumps pack four rotations into about half a second of air time, and once seemed physically out of reach.
Sports played on ice.Speed skating: Racers in the long-track version skate in pairs and swap lanes each lap, and the clap skate with a hinged blade shaved seconds off times in 1998.
Sports played on ice.Bandy: Bandy is sometimes called the ancestor of ice hockey; it is played with a ball on a soccer-sized sheet of ice and is big in Russia and Sweden.
Sports played on ice.Ringette: Invented in Canada in the 1960s for girls, it uses a straight stick and a rubber ring in place of a puck.
Sports played on ice.Ice dancing: Ice dancing differs from pairs skating: it emphasizes rhythm and footwork, and lifts are limited in height and length.
Sports played on ice.Bobsleigh: Bobsleigh runs on an ice track, and the sled can reach speeds beyond 130 km/h with a team that pushes before jumping in.
Sports played on ice.Luge: The sled for luge goes feet-first, and top riders exceed 140 km/h on an ice track while lying on their backs.
Sports played on ice.Skeleton: Skeleton riders go headfirst on an ice track at close to 130 km/h, with their chin just inches above the ice.
Sports played on ice.Broomball: Broomball is played on an ice rink with shoes instead of skates, using a broom-like stick and a ball.
Sports played on ice.Ski jumping: This one is on snow, not ice: ski jumpers fly off a ramp, and in ski flying the biggest hills carry them beyond 200 meters.
Sports played on ice.Biathlon: Biathlon mixes cross-country skiing with rifle shooting, and it happens on snow trails rather than on ice.
Sports played on ice.Snowboarding: A snowboard needs snow, not ice, and the sport's first Olympic appearance came in 1998 in Nagano.
Sports played on ice.Alpine skiing: Alpine skiing happens on snowy slopes, and downhill racers can reach 140 km/h on a mountain, nothing like an ice rink.
Sports played on ice.Cross-country skiing: Skiers cover a trail of snow, and in the longest events they race for 50 km or more across open terrain.
Sports played on ice.Field hockey: Field hockey is played on grass or artificial turf and has been an Olympic sport since 1908, but it never touches ice.
Sports played on ice.Roller derby: Roller derby is played on quad skates on a flat track, and it needs a hard floor, not ice.
Sports played on ice.Inline hockey: Inline hockey is played on wheels on a flat, hard surface rather than ice, which sets it apart from the ice version.
Sports played on ice.Bowling: Tenpin bowling happens on wooden or synthetic lanes oiled in patterns, and there's no ice involved.
Sports played on ice.Shuffleboard: Shuffleboard slides discs on a smooth court, often on cruise ships, and it is a dry-land game.
Sports played on ice.Water polo: Water polo is played in a pool, and the players have to tread water because the pool is too deep to stand in.
Sports played on ice.Sled dog racing: Dogs pull sleds across snow rather than ice, and the Iditarod covers about 1,000 miles of Alaska each March.
Sports played on ice.Freestyle skiing: Freestyle skiing, including moguls, takes place on snow slopes and not on ice rinks.

Hobbies where something flies.Kite flying: Kites were invented in China over 2,000 years ago. Benjamin Franklin's famous experiment with one helped show lightning is electrical.
Hobbies where something flies.Paragliding: A paraglider is a foot-launched fabric wing with no rigid frame, and pilots can ride rising air for hours to cross long distances.
Hobbies where something flies.Hang gliding: Hang glider pilots hang from a rigid triangular wing and steer by shifting body weight. Distance flights of hundreds of kilometers have been recorded.
Hobbies where something flies.Skydiving: Skydivers reach about 200 km/h (120 mph) in belly-to-earth free fall, then slow to a gentle glide once their parachute opens.
Hobbies where something flies.Drone racing: Pilots race small quadcopters through gates at speeds over 100 km/h while watching a live video feed through goggles, as if sitting aboard.
Hobbies where something flies.Hot air ballooning: Hot air balloons rise because heated air is less dense than the surrounding air. The first passengers, in 1783, were a sheep, a duck and a rooster.
Hobbies where something flies.Gliding: Sailplanes have no engine and can stay up for hours riding thermals. Pilots have flown more than 3,000 km in a single flight.
Hobbies where something flies.Model rocketry: Hobby rockets use pre-made solid motors and often return by parachute. The hobby's safety code dates to the 1950s.
Hobbies where something flies.Parasailing: A parasailer is towed behind a boat while hanging below a parachute-like canopy, rising to a few hundred feet above the water.
Hobbies where something flies.Paramotoring: A paramotor puts a propeller engine on a pilot's back and a paraglider wing overhead, so you can take off from flat ground, no hill needed.
Hobbies where something flies.Falconry: Falconry is an ancient art of hunting with trained raptors, recognized by UNESCO as cultural heritage. The bird is the one that flies.
Hobbies where something flies.Scuba diving: Scuba stands for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus. It's about moving through water, nothing flies.
Hobbies where something flies.Snorkeling: Snorkelers float at the surface breathing through a tube. They glide through water, and nothing here takes to the air.
Hobbies where something flies.Caving: Cavers explore underground passages, some of which stretch for hundreds of kilometers. Nothing flies, unless bats count.
Hobbies where something flies.Rock climbing: Climbers ascend on holds and use ropes only for safety; nothing in the sport takes flight.
Hobbies where something flies.Surfing: Surfers ride waves that began as wind-driven swells, sometimes traveling thousands of miles. Nothing leaves the water.
Hobbies where something flies.Kayaking: Kayaks were developed by the Inuit and Aleut as hunting boats made from skins over a frame. The paddler stays on the water.
Hobbies where something flies.Mountain biking: Riders may get airborne off jumps, but the bike isn't meant to fly. The sport grew in 1970s California on old balloon-tire bikes.
Hobbies where something flies.Trampolining: Trampolinists can launch over 8 meters high in competition, yet it's the body bouncing, with no flying object involved.
Hobbies where something flies.Sailing: Sailing uses wind but stays on water. Modern foiling boats lift their hulls out of the water, but that's skimming, not flying.
Hobbies where something flies.Ice skating: Skaters glide on a thin film of meltwater under the blade. Jumps get them briefly airborne, but nothing flies.
Hobbies where something flies.Fishing: One of humanity's oldest pursuits, fishing involves a line in the water, not objects in the air, unlike falconry.
Hobbies where something flies.Hiking: Hiking is walking on trails, and it keeps you firmly on the ground, no flight involved.
Hobbies where something flies.Horse riding: The horse may leap fences, but the sport isn't about anything flying. Horses can gallop at around 55 km/h.
